1 前言1 Preface

我在主要使用 C 和 C++ 达 25 年之后，开始学习 Racket。I learned Racket after 25 years of mostly using C and C++.

结果，脑子着实被甩了几下。Some psychic whiplash resulted.

“满眼都是括号”其实不是什么大问题。真正让我第一次脑筋打结的，是函数式编程。没过多久，我就想通了，随后也逐渐熟悉了 Racket 的许多其他方面和特性，用起来得心应手。"All the parentheses" was actually not a big deal. Instead, the first mind warp was functional programming. Before long I wrapped my brain around it, and went on to become comfortable and effective with many other aspects and features of Racket.

但还有两片最后的疆域尚未探索：宏和续延。But two final frontiers remained: Macros and continuations.

我发现，简单的宏很容易写，也不难理解，而且有很多不错的教程可看。但只要稍稍超出常规的模式匹配，我就像跌下悬崖，一头栽进了术语汤里。我把自己泡在各种资料中，希望多读几遍之后，这些知识终究能渗进脑子里。我甚至发现自己开始靠反复试错，而不是靠清晰的心智模型来理解究竟发生了什么。啊啊啊。I found that simple macros were easy and understandable, plus there were many good tutorials available. But the moment I stepped past routine pattern-matching, I kind of fell off a cliff into a terminology soup. I marinaded myself in material, hoping it would eventually sink in after enough re-readings. I even found myself using trial and error, rather than having a clear mental model what was going on. Gah.

如今，迷雾中的轮廓开始慢慢浮现，我也就开始动笔写这份指南了。I’m starting to write this at the point where the shapes are slowly emerging from the fog.

如果你有任何纠正、批评、抱怨，或是别的什么意见，请告诉我。If you have any corrections, criticisms, complaints, or whatever, please let me know.

我的首要动机其实很自私。把一件事解释清楚，会迫使我把它学得更透彻。而且，如果我写的东西有错，别人一定会迫不及待地指出来，帮我纠正。这算不算元编程的一种社会工程学变体？请问下一个问题。:)My primary motive is selfish. Explaining something forces me to learn it more thoroughly. Plus if I write something with mistakes, other people will be eager to point them out and correct me. Is that a social-engineering variation of meta-programming? Next question, please. :)

最后，我确实也希望它能帮助那些与我背景相似、学习方式相近，或两者兼有的人。Finally I do hope it may help other people who have a similar background and/or learning style as me.

我想展示 Racket 的宏特性是怎样为了解决各种问题或烦恼而演进的。当我找到自己已有疑问的答案，或找到自己已经切身感受到的问题的解决办法时，我会学得更快、更深入。因此，我会先把疑问和问题摆出来，让你能更好地体会和理解后面的答案与解决办法。I want to show how Racket macro features have evolved as solutions to problems or annoyances. I learn more quickly and deeply when I discover the answer to a question I already have, or find the solution to a problem whose pain I already feel. Therefore I’ll give you the questions and problems first, so that you can better appreciate and understand the answers and solutions.

2 我们的进攻计划2 Our plan of attack

要编写生产级的宏，你多半会想用一个叫作 syntax-parse 的宏系统。别担心，我们很快就会讲到它。The macro system you will mostly want to use for production-quality macros is called syntax-parse. And don’t worry, we’ll get to that soon.

不过，如果从那里开始，各种概念和术语很可能会让你招架不住，陷入迷茫。我就是这样。But if we start there, you’re likely to feel overwhelmed by concepts and terminology, and get very confused. I did.

1. 我们还是从基础开始吧：一个语法对象，以及一个用来改变它的函数——也就是“转换器”。我们会先在这个层面上练习一阵子，熟悉起来，也给宏这整套东西祛祛魅。1. Instead let’s start with the basics: A syntax object and a function to change it—a "transformer". We’ll work at that level for a while to get comfortable and to de-mythologize this whole macro business.

2. 很快，我们就会发现，模式匹配能让日子好过些。我们会学习 syntax-case 及其简写版亲戚 define-syntax-rule。我们还会发现，如果想先对模式变量做些处理，再把它们塞回模板里，很容易把自己绕晕；随后我们会学会该怎么做。2. Soon we’ll realize that pattern-matching would make life easier. We’ll learn about syntax-case and its shorthand cousin, define-syntax-rule. We’ll discover we can get confused if we want to munge pattern variables before sticking them back in the template, and learn how to do that.

3. 到这里，我们已经能写出许多有用的宏了。不过，如果想写一个一直很受欢迎、带有“魔法变量”的回指式 if 呢？原来，系统一直保护着我们，让我们不至于犯某类错误。如果我们偏偏想有意这么做，就要用语法参数。[还有其他更老的办法能做到这一点。我们不会介绍它们，也不会花很多时间鼓吹“卫生性”——就约定它是个好东西吧。]3. At this point we’ll be able to write many useful macros. But, what if we want to write the ever-popular anaphoric if, with a "magic variable"? It turns out we’ve been protected from making certain kind of mistakes. When we want to do this kind of thing on purpose, we use a syntax parameter. [There are other, older ways to do this. We won’t look at them. We also won’t spend a lot of time advocating "hygiene"—we’ll just stipulate that it’s good.]

4. 最后，我们会意识到，当宏被错误地使用时，它们本可以表现得更聪明一些。普通的 Racket 函数可以选择使用契约和类型。它们能发现使用上的错误，并给出清晰、有用的错误信息。要是宏也有类似的东西就好了。还真有。syntax-parse 就是 Racket 宏系统中较新的一项改进。4. Finally, we’ll realize that our macros could be smarter when they’re used in error. Normal Racket functions optionally can have contracts and types. These catch usage mistakes and provide clear, useful error messages. It would be great if there were something similar for macro. There is. One of the more-recent Racket macro enhancements is syntax-parse.

3 变形！3 Transform!

  YOU ARE INSIDE A ROOM.

  THERE ARE KEYS ON THE GROUND.

  THERE IS A SHINY BRASS LAMP NEARBY.

  

  IF YOU GO THE WRONG WAY, YOU WILL BECOME

  HOPELESSLY LOST AND CONFUSED.

  

  > pick up the keys

  

  YOU HAVE A SYNTAX TRANSFORMER

3.1 什么是语法转换器？3.1 What is a syntax transformer?

语法转换器可不是トランスフォーマ里的变形金刚。A syntax transformer is not one of the トランスフォーマ transformers.

它其实只是一个函数。这个函数接收语法，返回语法。它对语法进行转换。Instead, it is simply a function. The function takes syntax and returns syntax. It transforms syntax.

下面这个转换器函数会忽略输入的语法，始终输出一个字符串字面量的语法：Here’s a transformer function that ignores its input syntax, and always outputs syntax for a string literal:

这些示例都假定使用 #lang racket。如果你想在 #lang racket/base 中尝试它们，就需要 (require (for-syntax racket/base))。These examples assume #lang racket. If you want to try them using #lang racket/base, you’ll need to (require (for-syntax racket/base)).

> (define-syntax foo
    (lambda (stx)
      (syntax "I am foo")))

使用它：Using it:

> (foo)

"I am foo"

使用 define-syntax 时，我们是在建立一个转换器绑定。这相当于告诉 Racket 编译器：“只要遇到一块以 foo 开头的语法，就请把它交给我的转换器函数，并用我返回的语法替换它。”因此，Racket 会把任何形如 (foo ...) 的东西交给我们的函数，而我们可以返回新的语法来替代它。很像查找并替换。When we use define-syntax, we’re making a transformer binding. This tells the Racket compiler, "Whenever you encounter a chunk of syntax starting with foo, please give it to my transformer function, and replace it with the syntax I give back to you." So Racket will give anything that looks like (foo ...) to our function, and we can return new syntax to use instead. Much like a search-and-replace.

也许你知道，在 Racket 中定义函数的常见写法：Maybe you know that the usual way to define a function in Racket:

(define (f x) ...)

其实是下面这种写法的简写：is shorthand for:

(define f (lambda (x) ...))

这种简写让你可以少敲一个 lambda 和几个括号。That shorthand lets you avoid typing lambda and some parentheses.

嗯，define-syntax 也有类似的简写：Well there is a similar shorthand for define-syntax:

> (define-syntax (also-foo stx)
    (syntax "I am also foo"))
> (also-foo)

"I am also foo"

我们要记住，这仅仅是一种简写。我们仍然是在定义一个转换器函数，它接收语法并返回语法。我们用宏做的所有事情，都建立在这个基本思想之上。这不是什么魔法。What we want to remember is that this is simply shorthand. We are still defining a transformer function, which takes syntax and returns syntax. Everything we do with macros, will be built on top of this basic idea. It’s not magic.

说到简写，syntax 也有一种简写，就是 #'：Speaking of shorthand, there is also a shorthand for syntax, which is #':

#' 是 syntax 的简写，就像 ' 是 quote 的简写一样。#' is short for syntax much like ' is short for quote.

> (define-syntax (quoted-foo stx)
    #'"I am also foo, using #' instead of syntax")
> (quoted-foo)

"I am also foo, using #' instead of syntax"

从现在起，我们会使用 #' 这种简写。We’ll use the #' shorthand from now on.

当然，我们也可以生成比字符串字面量更有意思的语法。返回 (displayln "hi") 怎么样？Of course, we can emit syntax that is more interesting than a string literal. How about returning (displayln "hi")?

> (define-syntax (say-hi stx)
    #'(displayln "hi"))
> (say-hi)

hi

Racket 展开我们的程序时，会看到出现的 (say-hi)，并发现有对应的转换器函数。它用旧的语法调用我们的函数，而我们返回新的语法，用于程序的求值和运行。When Racket expands our program, it sees the occurrence of (say-hi), and sees it has a transformer function for that. It calls our function with the old syntax, and we return the new syntax, which is used to evaluate and run our program.

3.2 输入是什么？3.2 What’s the input?

到目前为止，我们的示例都忽略了输入的语法，只输出一些固定的语法。但通常，我们会想把输入的语法转换成别的东西。Our examples so far have ignored the input syntax and output some fixed syntax. But typically we will want to transform the input syntax into something else.

我们先来仔细看看，输入究竟是什么：Let’s start by looking closely at what the input actually is:

> (define-syntax (show-me stx)
    (print stx)
    #'(void))
> (show-me '(+ 1 2))

#<syntax:eval:10:0 (show-me (quote (+ 1 2)))>

(print stx) 展示了传给转换器的东西：一个语法对象。The (print stx) shows what our transformer is given: a syntax object.

语法对象由几部分组成。第一部分是表示代码的 S 表达式，例如 '(+ 1 2)。A syntax object consists of several things. The first part is the S-expression representing the code, such as '(+ 1 2).

Racket 的语法还附带一些有意思的信息，比如源文件、行号和列号。最后，它还包含词法作用域的信息（你现在不必操心这个，不过后面它会变得很重要）。Racket syntax is also decorated with some interesting information such as the source file, line number, and column. Finally, it has information about lexical scoping (which you don’t need to worry about now, but will turn out to be important later.)

有各种各样的函数可以访问语法对象。我们先定义一段语法：There are a variety of functions available to access a syntax object. Let’s define a piece of syntax:

> (define stx #'(if x (list "true") #f))
> stx

#<syntax:eval:11:0 (if x (list "true") #f)>

现在，我们来使用访问语法对象的函数。获取源代码信息的函数有：Now let’s use functions that access the syntax object. The source information functions are:

(syntax-source stx) 之所以返回 'eval，只是因为我生成这份文档时，是用一个求值器来运行 Scribble 中的代码片段。通常，这里会是类似 "my-file.rkt" 的东西。(syntax-source stx) is returning 'eval, only because of how I’m generating this documentation, using an evaluator to run code snippets in Scribble. Normally this would be something like "my-file.rkt".

> (syntax-source stx)

'eval

> (syntax-line stx)

11

> (syntax-column stx)

0

更有意思的是语法本身的“内容”。syntax->datum 会把它完整地转换成一个 S 表达式：More interesting is the syntax "stuff" itself. syntax->datum converts it completely into an S-expression:

> (syntax->datum stx)

'(if x (list "true") #f)

而 syntax-e 只会“向下一层”。它返回的可能是一个包含语法对象的列表：Whereas syntax-e only goes "one level down". It may return a list that has syntax objects:

> (syntax-e stx)

'(#<syntax:eval:11:0 if> #<syntax:eval:11:0 x> #<syntax:eval:11:0 (list "true")> #<syntax:eval:11:0 #f>)

其中每个语法对象又都可以用 syntax-e 转换，如此递归下去——这正是 syntax->datum 所做的事。Each of those syntax objects could be converted by syntax-e, and so on recursively—which is what syntax->datum does.

大多数情况下，syntax->list 给出的结果与 syntax-e 相同：In most cases, syntax->list gives the same result as syntax-e:

> (syntax->list stx)

'(#<syntax:eval:11:0 if> #<syntax:eval:11:0 x> #<syntax:eval:11:0 (list "true")> #<syntax:eval:11:0 #f>)

（syntax-e 和 syntax->list 什么时候会不同呢？我们先别岔开话题。）(When would syntax-e and syntax->list differ? Let’s not get side-tracked now.)

要转换语法时，我们通常会取出收到的各个部分，也许重新排列它们的顺序，也许修改其中一些部分，而且经常会引入全新的部分。When we want to transform syntax, we’ll generally take the pieces we were given, maybe rearrange their order, perhaps change some of the pieces, and often introduce brand-new pieces.

3.3 真正动手转换输入3.3 Actually transforming the input

我们来写一个转换器函数，把收到的语法倒过来：Let’s write a transformer function that reverses the syntax it was given:

示例末尾的 values 能让结果顺利求值。试试 (reverse-me "backwards" "am" "i")，就知道它为什么方便了。The values at the end of the example allows the result to evaluate nicely. Try (reverse-me "backwards" "am" "i") to see why it’s handy.

> (define-syntax (reverse-me stx)
    (datum->syntax stx (reverse (cdr (syntax->datum stx)))))
> (reverse-me "backwards" "am" "i" values)

"i"

"am"

"backwards"

尤达的话，听懂我们能。很好，不过这是怎么做到的呢？Understand Yoda, we can. Great, but how does this work?

首先，我们取出输入的语法，交给 syntax->datum。它会把语法转换成一个普普通通的列表：First we take the input syntax, and give it to syntax->datum. This converts the syntax into a plain old list:

> (syntax->datum #'(reverse-me "backwards" "am" "i" values))

'(reverse-me "backwards" "am" "i" values)

用 cdr 去掉列表的第一项 reverse-me，剩下的就是：("backwards" "am" "i" values)。把它交给 reverse，就会变成 (values "i" "am" "backwards")：Using cdr slices off the first item of the list, reverse-me, leaving the remainder: ("backwards" "am" "i" values). Passing that to reverse changes it to (values "i" "am" "backwards"):

> (reverse (cdr '(reverse-me "backwards" "am" "i" values)))

'(values "i" "am" "backwards")

最后，我们用 datum->syntax 把它转换回 syntax：Finally we use datum->syntax to convert this back to syntax:

> (datum->syntax #f '(values "i" "am" "backwards"))

#<syntax (values "i" "am" "backwards")>

这就是我们的转换器函数交还给 Racket 编译器的东西，随后这段语法会被求值：That’s what our transformer function gives back to the Racket compiler, and that syntax is evaluated:

> (values "i" "am" "backwards")

"i"

"am"

"backwards"

datum->syntax 的第一个参数包含词法上下文信息，我们希望将这些信息关联到转换器输出的 syntax 上。如果第一个参数设为 #f，就不会关联任何词法上下文。The first argument of datum->syntax contains the lexical context information that we want to associate with the syntax outputted by the transformer. If the first argument is set to #f then no lexical context will be associated.

3.4 编译时与运行时3.4 Compile time vs. run time

(define-syntax (foo stx)
  (make-pipe) ;Ce n'est pas le temps d'exécution
  #'(void))

普通的 Racket 代码在……运行时运行。废话。Normal Racket code runs at ... run time. Duh.

除了“编译时与运行时”，你可能还会听到另一种说法：“语法阶段与运行阶段”。说的都是一回事。Instead of "compile time vs. run time", you may hear it described as "syntax phase vs. runtime phase". Same difference.

但语法转换器是由 Racket 在解析、展开和编译程序的过程中调用的。换句话说，我们的语法转换器函数是在编译时求值的。But a syntax transformer is called by Racket as part of the process of parsing, expanding, and compiling our program. In other words, our syntax transformer function is evaluated at compile time.

宏的这一特点使你能做到一些普通代码根本做不到的事。一个经典的例子，就是类似 Racket 的 if 这样的形式：This aspect of macros lets you do things that simply aren’t possible in normal code. One of the classic examples is something like the Racket form, if:

(if <condition> <true-expression> <false-expression>)

如果我们把 if 实现为函数，那么所有实参都会在传给函数之前被求值。If we implemented if as a function, all of the arguments would be evaluated before being provided to the function.

> (define (our-if condition true-expr false-expr)
    (cond [condition true-expr]
          [else false-expr]))
> (our-if #t
          "true"
          "false")

"true"

看起来能用。不过，这样呢：That seems to work. However, how about this:

> (define (display-and-return x)
    (displayln x)
    x)
> (our-if #t
          (display-and-return "true")
          (display-and-return "false"))

true

false

"true"

一种回答是：函数式编程是好的，副作用是坏的。但要避免副作用，并不总是现实。One answer is that functional programming is good, and side-effects are bad. But avoiding side-effects isn’t always practical.

哎呀。由于这些表达式有副作用，很明显，它们都被求值了。这可能会出问题——要是副作用包括删除磁盘上的文件呢？你可不希望即使 user-wants-file-deleted? 为 #f，(if user-wants-file-deleted? (delete-file) (void)) 也照样删除文件。Oops. Because the expressions have a side-effect, it’s obvious that they are both evaluated. And that could be a problem—what if the side-effect includes deleting a file on disk? You wouldn’t want (if user-wants-file-deleted? (delete-file) (void)) to delete a file even when user-wants-file-deleted? is #f.

所以，把它做成一个普通函数根本行不通。不过，语法转换器可以在编译时重新排列语法——也就是改写代码。各块语法只是被挪来挪去，直到运行时才会真正求值。So this simply can’t work as a plain function. However a syntax transformer can rearrange the syntax – rewrite the code – at compile time. The pieces of syntax are moved around, but they aren’t actually evaluated until run time.

下面是实现它的一种方法：Here is one way to do this:

> (define-syntax (our-if-v2 stx)
    (define xs (syntax->list stx))
    (datum->syntax stx `(cond [,(cadr xs) ,(caddr xs)]
                              [else ,(cadddr xs)])))
> (our-if-v2 #t
             (display-and-return "true")
             (display-and-return "false"))

true

"true"

> (our-if-v2 #f
             (display-and-return "true")
             (display-and-return "false"))

false

"false"

这给出了正确答案。不过，为什么呢？我们把转换器函数本身单独拿出来，看看它做了什么。先举一段输入语法作为例子：That gave the right answer. But how? Let’s pull out the transformer function itself, and see what it did. We start with an example of some input syntax:

> (define stx #'(our-if-v2 #t "true" "false"))
> (displayln stx)

#<syntax:eval:32:0 (our-if-v2 #t "true" "false")>

1. 我们取出原来的语法，用 syntax->list 把它变成一个由语法对象组成的 list：1. We take the original syntax, and use syntax->list to change it into a list of syntax objects:

> (define xs (syntax->list stx))
> (displayln xs)

(#<syntax:eval:32:0 our-if-v2> #<syntax:eval:32:0 #t> #<syntax:eval:32:0 "true"> #<syntax:eval:32:0 "false">)

2. 要把它变成 Racket 的 cond 形式，我们需要用 cadr、caddr 和 cadddr 从列表中取出三个关键部分——条件、条件为真时的表达式，以及条件为假时的表达式——并将它们组织成一个 cond 形式：2. To change this into a Racket cond form, we need to take the three interesting pieces—the condition, true-expression, and false-expression—from the list using cadr, caddr, and cadddr and arrange them into a cond form:

`(cond [,(cadr xs) ,(caddr xs)]
       [else ,(cadddr xs)])

3. 最后，我们用 datum->syntax 把它变成 syntax：3. Finally, we change that into syntax using datum->syntax:

> (datum->syntax stx `(cond [,(cadr xs) ,(caddr xs)]
                            [else ,(cadddr xs)]))

#<syntax (cond (#t "true") (else "false"))>

这样能用，但用 cadddr 等函数来解构列表，既痛苦又容易出错。也许你知道 Racket 的 match？用它就能做模式匹配了。So that works, but using cadddr etc. to destructure a list is painful and error-prone. Maybe you know Racket’s match? Using that would let us do pattern-matching.

注意，我们并不关心语法列表的第一项。在 our-if-v2 中，我们没有取 (car xs)；使用模式匹配时，我们也没有用到 name。一般来说，语法转换器不会关心它，因为它是转换器绑定的名称。换句话说，宏通常并不在乎自己叫什么。Notice that we don’t care about the first item in the syntax list. We didn’t take (car xs) in our-if-v2, and we didn’t use name when we used pattern-matching. In general, a syntax transformer won’t care about that, because it is the name of the transformer binding. In other words, a macro usually doesn’t care about its own name.

不用这样写：Instead of:

> (define-syntax (our-if-v2 stx)
    (define xs (syntax->list stx))
    (datum->syntax stx `(cond [,(cadr xs) ,(caddr xs)]
                              [else ,(cadddr xs)])))

我们可以这样写：We can write:

> (define-syntax (our-if-using-match stx)
    (match (syntax->list stx)
      [(list name condition true-expr false-expr)
       (datum->syntax stx `(cond [,condition ,true-expr]
                                 [else ,false-expr]))]))

很好。现在来试着用用它：Great. Now let’s try using it:

> (our-if-using-match #t "true" "false")

match: undefined;

 cannot reference an identifier before its definition

  in module: 'program

哎呀。它抱怨说 match 没有定义。Oops. It’s complaining that match isn’t defined.

我们的转换器函数在编译时工作，而不是在运行时。在编译时，系统只会自动为你引入 racket/base，而不是完整的 racket。Our transformer function is working at compile time, not run time. And at compile time, only racket/base is required for you automatically—not the full racket.

凡是超出 racket/base 的部分，都得由我们自己引入——而且要使用 require 的 for-syntax 形式，在编译时引入。Anything beyond racket/base, we have to require ourselves—and require it for compile time using the for-syntax form of require.

这里，我们想要的不是普通的 (require racket/match)，而是 (require (for-syntax racket/match))——其中的 for-syntax 表示“供编译时使用”。In this case, instead of using plain (require racket/match), we want (require (for-syntax racket/match))—the for-syntax part meaning, "for compile time".

那就来试试：So let’s try that:

> (require (for-syntax racket/match))
> (define-syntax (our-if-using-match-v2 stx)
    (match (syntax->list stx)
      [(list _ condition true-expr false-expr)
       (datum->syntax stx `(cond [,condition ,true-expr]
                                 [else ,false-expr]))]))
> (our-if-using-match-v2 #t "true" "false")

"true"

太棒了。Joy.

3.5 begin-for-syntax

我们用 for-syntax 来 require 模块 racket/match，是因为我们需要在编译时使用 match。We used for-syntax to require the racket/match module because we needed to use match at compile time.

如果我们想定义自己的辅助函数，供宏使用呢？一种办法是把它放在另一个模块里，再用 for-syntax 来 require 它，就像我们对 racket/match 模块所做的那样。What if we wanted to define our own helper function to be used by a macro? One way to do that is put it in another module, and require it using for-syntax, just like we did with the racket/match module.

如果想把辅助函数放在同一个模块里，就不能简单地用 define 定义它然后直接使用——这样定义会存在于运行时，而我们需要的是在编译时使用它。解决办法是把辅助函数的定义放在 begin-for-syntax 里面：If instead we want to put the helper in the same module, we can’t simply define it and use it—the definition would exist at run time, but we need it at compile time. The answer is to put the definition of the helper function(s) inside begin-for-syntax:

(begin-for-syntax
 (define (my-helper-function ....)
   ....))
(define-syntax (macro-using-my-helper-function stx)
  (my-helper-function ....)
  ....)

在简单的情况下，我们也可以使用 define-for-syntax，它将 begin-for-syntax 和 define 合在了一起：In the simple case, we can also use define-for-syntax, which composes begin-for-syntax and define:

(define-for-syntax (my-helper-function ....)
  ....)
(define-syntax (macro-using-my-helper-function stx)
  (my-helper-function ....)
  ....)

回顾一下：To review:

  • 语法转换器在编译时工作，而不是在运行时。好消息是，这意味着我们可以重新排列各块语法，而不对它们求值。我们可以实现 if 这样的形式；若把它们做成运行时的函数，根本无法正常工作。Syntax transformers work at compile time, not run time. The good news is this means we can do things like rearrange the pieces of syntax without evaluating them. We can implement forms like if that simply couldn’t work properly as run time functions.

  • 另一个好消息是，编写语法转换器并不需要某种特殊而古怪的语言。我们可以用早已熟悉并喜爱的 Racket 语言来编写这些转换器函数。More good news is that there isn’t some special, weird language for writing syntax transformers. We can write these transformer functions using the Racket language we already know and love.

  • 有一点算不上太坏的坏消息是，这种熟悉感很容易让人忘记：我们并不是在运行时工作。有时，记住这一点很重要。The semi-bad news is that the familiarity can make it easy to forget that we’re not working at run time. Sometimes that’s important to remember.

    • 例如，系统只会自动为我们引入 racket/base。如果还需要其他模块，就得自己引入，而且要使用 for-syntax 在编译时引入它们。For example only racket/base is required for us automatically. If we need other modules, we have to require them, and do so for compile time using for-syntax.

    • 同样，如果我们想把辅助函数定义在使用它们的宏所在的文件或模块中，就需要用 begin-for-syntax 形式把这些定义包起来。这样，它们就能在编译时使用了。Similarly, if we want to define helper functions in the same file/module as the macros that use them, we need to wrap the definitions inside a begin-for-syntax form. Doing so makes them available at compile time.

4 模式匹配：syntax-case 与 syntax-rules4 Pattern matching: syntax-case and syntax-rules

大多数实用的语法转换器，都是接收一些输入语法，再把其中的各个部分重新排列成别的东西。正如我们看到的，用 cadddr 这样的列表访问器可以做到这一点，但很繁琐。使用 match 进行模式匹配更方便，也更不容易出错。Most useful syntax transformers work by taking some input syntax, and rearranging the pieces into something else. As we saw, this is possible but tedious using list accessors such as cadddr. It’s more convenient and less error-prone to use match to do pattern-matching.

从历史上看，先有了 syntax-case 和 syntax-rules 的模式匹配。match 是后来才加入 Racket 的。Historically, syntax-case and syntax-rules pattern matching came first. match was added to Racket later.

原来，模式匹配是 Racket 宏系统最早加入的改进之一。它叫作 syntax-case，还有一个适用于简单情况的简写形式，叫作 define-syntax-rule。It turns out that pattern-matching was one of the first improvements to be added to the Racket macro system. It’s called syntax-case, and has a shorthand for simple situations called define-syntax-rule.

回顾一下我们之前的例子：Recall our previous example:

(require (for-syntax racket/match))
(define-syntax (our-if-using-match-v2 stx)
  (match (syntax->list stx)
    [(list _ condition true-expr false-expr)
     (datum->syntax stx `(cond [,condition ,true-expr]
                               [else ,false-expr]))]))

用 syntax-case 来写是这样的：Here’s what it looks like using syntax-case:

> (define-syntax (our-if-using-syntax-case stx)
    (syntax-case stx ()
      [(_ condition true-expr false-expr)
       #'(cond [condition true-expr]
               [else false-expr])]))
> (our-if-using-syntax-case #t "true" "false")

"true"

很像，对吧？模式匹配的部分看起来几乎一模一样。指定新语法的方式则更简单了。我们不需要使用准引用和取消引用，也不需要使用 datum->syntax。取而代之的是提供一个“模板”，其中使用模式里的变量。Pretty similar, huh? The pattern matching part looks almost exactly the same. The way we specify the new syntax is simpler. We don’t need to do quasi-quoting and unquoting. We don’t need to use datum->syntax. Instead, we supply a "template", which uses variables from the pattern.

对于简单的模式匹配情况，有一种会展开为 syntax-case 的简写形式，叫作 define-syntax-rule：There is a shorthand for simple pattern-matching cases, which expands into syntax-case. It’s called define-syntax-rule:

> (define-syntax-rule (our-if-using-syntax-rule condition true-expr false-expr)
    (cond [condition true-expr]
          [else false-expr]))
> (our-if-using-syntax-rule #t "true" "false")

"true"

关于 define-syntax-rule，有这么个问题。因为它如此简单，define-syntax-rule 往往是人们学习宏时接触的第一个东西。但它简单得几乎具有迷惑性。它看起来太像在定义一个普通的运行时函数了——然而并不是。它工作在编译时，而不是运行时。更糟的是，一旦你想做的事情超出了 define-syntax-rule 的能力范围，就可能一下跌落悬崖，掉进一片感觉既复杂又令人困惑的天地。但愿我们不会遇到这个问题，因为我们是从基本的语法转换器开始，一步步走过来的。我们可以欣赏 define-syntax-rule 作为一种便捷简写的好处，同时不必害怕或困惑于它所简写的东西。Here’s the thing about define-syntax-rule. Because it’s so simple, define-syntax-rule is often the first thing people are taught about macros. But it’s almost deceptively simple. It looks so much like defining a normal run time function—yet it’s not. It’s working at compile time, not run time. Worse, the moment you want to do more than define-syntax-rule can handle, you can fall off a cliff into what feels like complicated and confusing territory. Hopefully, because we started with a basic syntax transformer, and worked up from that, we won’t have that problem. We can appreciate define-syntax-rule as a convenient shorthand, but not be scared of, or confused about, that for which it’s shorthand.

我找到的大多数宏学习资料，包括《Racket 指南》，都把模式和模板的工作原理解释得很好。所以这里我就不再重复了。Most of the materials I found for learning macros, including the Racket Guide, do a very good job explaining how patterns and templates work. So I won’t regurgitate that here.

有时，我们需要在模式和模板之外再多走一步。让我们看几个例子，看看我们会怎样陷入困惑，又该怎样让它正常工作。Sometimes, we need to go a step beyond the pattern and template. Let’s look at some examples, how we can get confused, and how to get it working.

4.1 模式变量对阵模板——开打！4.1 Pattern variable vs. template—fight!

假设我们想定义一个名字带连字符的函数 a-b，但分别提供 a 和 b 这两个部分。Racket 的 struct 宏就会做类似的事情：(struct foo (field1 field2)) 会自动定义若干函数，它们的名字都是 foo 这个名字的变体——比如 foo-field1、foo-field2、foo?，等等。Let’s say we want to define a function with a hyphenated name, a-b, but we supply the a and b parts separately. The Racket struct macro does something like this: (struct foo (field1 field2)) automatically defines a number of functions whose names are variations on the name foo—such as foo-field1, foo-field2, foo?, and so on.

那么，就假设我们也在做类似的事情。我们想把语法 (hyphen-define a b (args) body) 转换成语法 (define (a-b args) body)。So let’s pretend we’re doing something like that. We want to transform the syntax (hyphen-define a b (args) body) to the syntax (define (a-b args) body).

第一次尝试写错了，是这样的：A wrong first attempt is:

> (define-syntax (hyphen-define/wrong1 stx)
    (syntax-case stx ()
      [(_ a b (args ...) body0 body ...)
       (let ([name (string->symbol (format "~a-~a" a b))])
         #'(define (name args ...)
             body0 body ...))]))

eval:47:0: a: pattern variable cannot be used outside of a

template

  in: a

咦。我们完全不知道这条错误消息是什么意思。好吧，试着弄明白它。错误消息所说的“模板”，指的是 #'(define (name args ...) body0 body ...) 这一部分。let 不属于那个模板。听起来，我们不能在 let 部分使用 a（或 b）。Huh. We have no idea what this error message means. Well, let’s try to work it out. The "template" the error message refers to is the #'(define (name args ...) body0 body ...) portion. The let isn’t part of that template. It sounds like we can’t use a (or b) in the let part.

实际上，syntax-case 里想放多少个模板都可以。最明显、也必不可少的模板，是提供输出语法的最后一个表达式。但你也可以对模式变量使用 syntax（也就是 #'）。这样就又创建了一个模板，只不过它是个小小的“迷你装”模板。我们来试试：In fact, syntax-case can have as many templates as you want. The obvious, required template is the final expression supplying the output syntax. But you can use syntax (a.k.a. #') on a pattern variable. This makes another template, albeit a small, "fun size" template. Let’s try that:

> (define-syntax (hyphen-define/wrong1.1 stx)
    (syntax-case stx ()
      [(_ a b (args ...) body0 body ...)
       (let ([name (string->symbol (format "~a-~a" #'a #'b))])
         #'(define (name args ...)
             body0 body ...))]))

不再报错了——很好！来试着用用它：No more errors—good! Let’s try to use it:

> (hyphen-define/wrong1.1 foo bar () #t)
> (foo-bar)

foo-bar: undefined;

 cannot reference an identifier before its definition

  in module: 'program

看来，我们的宏定义了一个函数，但名字并不是 foo-bar。咦。Apparently our macro is defining a function with some name other than foo-bar. Huh.

这种时候，DrRacket 中的宏步进器就无比宝贵了。This is where the Macro Stepper in DrRacket is invaluable.

即便你平时更喜欢用 Emacs，遇到这种情况，也绝对值得暂时用一下 DrRacket，就为了它的宏步进器。Even if you prefer mostly to use Emacs, this is a situation where it’s definitely worth temporarily using DrRacket for its Macro Stepper.

宏步进器显示，我们的这次宏使用：The Macro Stepper says that the use of our macro:

(hyphen-define/wrong1.1 foo bar () #t)

展开成了：expanded to:

(define (name) #t)

好吧，这就解释得通了。但我们想要的是展开成：Well that explains it. Instead, we wanted to expand to:

(define (foo-bar) #t)

我们的模板使用的是符号 name，但我们想要的是它的值，比如这次使用宏时的 foo-bar。Our template is using the symbol name but we wanted its value, such as foo-bar in this use of our macro.

我们已经知道的东西里，有没有什么就具备这种行为——在模板中使用一个变量，就会得到它的值？有：模式变量。我们的模式不包含 name，因为我们并不期望原始语法中有它——事实上，这个宏的全部目的就是创建它。所以 name 不能放在主模式里。没关系——我们再创建一个模式。只要再嵌套一层 syntax-case 就可以了：Is there anything we already know that behaves like this—where using a variable in the template yields its value? Yes: Pattern variables. Our pattern doesn’t include name because we don’t expect it in the original syntax—indeed the whole point of this macro is to create it. So name can’t be in the main pattern. Fine—let’s make an additional pattern. We can do that using an additional, nested syntax-case:

> (define-syntax (hyphen-define/wrong1.2 stx)
    (syntax-case stx ()
      [(_ a b (args ...) body0 body ...)
       (syntax-case (datum->syntax #'a
                                   (string->symbol (format "~a-~a" #'a #'b)))
                    ()
         [name #'(define (name args ...)
                   body0 body ...)])]))

看起来很奇怪？深呼吸一下。通常，Racket 会把语法交给我们的转换器函数，然后我们再把这份语法传给 syntax-case。但我们也可以临时创建自己的语法，再把它传给 syntax-case。这里做的事情仅此而已。整个 (datum->syntax ...) 表达式，就是我们临时创建的语法。我们可以把它交给 syntax-case，用一个名叫 name 的模式变量来匹配它。瞧，我们就有了一个新的模式变量。我们可以在模板中使用它，它的值就会填进模板。Looks weird? Let’s take a deep breath. Normally our transformer function is given syntax by Racket, and we pass that syntax to syntax-case. But we can also create some syntax of our own, on the fly, and pass that to syntax-case. That’s all we’re doing here. The whole (datum->syntax ...) expression is syntax that we’re creating on the fly. We can give that to syntax-case, and match it using a pattern variable named name. Voila, we have a new pattern variable. We can use it in a template, and its value will go in the template.

我们可能还剩一个小问题——就一个，我保证！来试试新版本：We might have one more—just one, I promise!—small problem left. Let’s try to use our new version:

> (hyphen-define/wrong1.2 foo bar () #t)
> (foo-bar)

foo-bar: undefined;

 cannot reference an identifier before its definition

  in module: 'program

嗯。foo-bar 还是没有定义。再回到宏步进器。它显示，现在我们展开成了：Hmm. foo-bar is still not defined. Back to the Macro Stepper. It says now we’re expanding to:

(define (|#<syntax:11:24foo>-#<syntax:11:28 bar>|) #t)

哦，对了：#'a 和 #'b 都是语法对象。因此，Oh right: #'a and #'b are syntax objects. Therefore

(string->symbol (format "~a-~a" #'a #'b))

就是这两个语法对象的打印形式，用连字符连接了起来：is the printed form of both syntax objects, joined by a hyphen:

|#<syntax:11:24foo>-#<syntax:11:28 bar>|

但我们想要的是语法对象中的基准数据，比如符号 foo 和 bar。用 syntax->datum 就能得到：Instead we want the datum in the syntax objects, such as the symbols foo and bar. Which we get using syntax->datum:

> (define-syntax (hyphen-define/ok1 stx)
    (syntax-case stx ()
      [(_ a b (args ...) body0 body ...)
       (syntax-case (datum->syntax #'a
                                   (string->symbol (format "~a-~a"
                                                           (syntax->datum #'a)
                                                           (syntax->datum #'b))))
                    ()
         [name #'(define (name args ...)
                   body0 body ...)])]))
> (hyphen-define/ok1 foo bar () #t)
> (foo-bar)

#t

现在终于能用了！And now it works!

接下来，介绍几个简便写法。Next, some shortcuts.

4.1.1 with-syntax

除了再嵌套一层 syntax-case，我们也可以使用 with-syntax。它把 syntax-case 重新排列成更像 let 语句的样子——先是名字，然后是值。另外，如果我们需要定义不止一个模式变量，它也更方便。Instead of an additional, nested syntax-case, we could use with-syntax. This rearranges the syntax-case to look more like a let statement—first the name, then the value. Also it’s more convenient if we need to define more than one pattern variable.

with-syntax 还可以换个名字，叫作“引入新的模式变量”。Another name for with-syntax could be, "with new pattern variable".
> (define-syntax (hyphen-define/ok2 stx)
    (syntax-case stx ()
      [(_ a b (args ...) body0 body ...)
       (with-syntax ([name (datum->syntax #'a
                                          (string->symbol (format "~a-~a"
                                                                  (syntax->datum #'a)
                                                                  (syntax->datum #'b))))])
         #'(define (name args ...)
             body0 body ...))]))
> (hyphen-define/ok2 foo bar () #t)
> (foo-bar)

#t

再强调一次，with-syntax 就是重新排列后的 syntax-case：Again, with-syntax is simply syntax-case rearranged:

(syntax-case <syntax> () [<pattern> <body>])
(with-syntax ([<pattern> <syntax>]) <body>)

无论是再用一个 syntax-case，还是使用 with-syntax，你所做的都只是定义额外的模式变量。别让术语和结构把这件事弄得神秘兮兮的。Whether you use an additional syntax-case or use with-syntax, either way you are simply defining additional pattern variables. Don’t let the terminology and structure make it seem mysterious.

4.1.2 with-syntax*

我们知道，let 不允许在后续绑定中使用前面的绑定：We know that let doesn’t let us use a binding in a subsequent one:

> (let ([a 0]
        [b a])
    b)

a: undefined;

 cannot reference an identifier before its definition

  in module: 'program

我们可以改为嵌套使用 let：Instead we can nest lets:

> (let ([a 0])
    (let ([b a])
      b))

0

或者使用这种嵌套的简写形式 let*：Or use a shorthand for nesting, let*:

> (let* ([a 0]
         [b a])
    b)

0

同样，我们也可以用 with-syntax*，而不必嵌套编写 with-syntax：Similarly, instead of writing nested with-syntaxs, we can use with-syntax*:

> (require (for-syntax racket/syntax))
> (define-syntax (foo stx)
    (syntax-case stx ()
      [(_ a)
        (with-syntax* ([b #'a]
                       [c #'b])
          #'c)]))

有个陷阱：with-syntax* 并不由 racket/base 提供。我们必须写上 (require (for-syntax racket/syntax))。否则，可能会得到一条相当令人摸不着头脑的错误消息：One gotcha is that with-syntax* isn’t provided by racket/base. We must (require (for-syntax racket/syntax)). Otherwise we may get a rather bewildering error message:

...: ellipses not allowed as an expression in: ....

4.1.3 format-id

racket/syntax 中有一个名叫 format-id 的工具函数，能让我们以比上面更简洁的方式格式化标识符名字：There is a utility function in racket/syntax called format-id that lets us format identifier names more succinctly than what we did above:

> (require (for-syntax racket/syntax))
> (define-syntax (hyphen-define/ok3 stx)
    (syntax-case stx ()
      [(_ a b (args ...) body0 body ...)
       (with-syntax ([name (format-id #'a "~a-~a" #'a #'b)])
         #'(define (name args ...)
             body0 body ...))]))
> (hyphen-define/ok3 bar baz () #t)
> (bar-baz)

#t

使用 format-id 很方便，因为它会帮我们完成从语法到符号基准数据，再到字符串……然后一路转换回来的繁琐工作。Using format-id is convenient as it handles the tedium of converting from syntax to symbol datum to string ... and all the way back.

format-id 的第一个参数 lctx，是将要创建的标识符的词法上下文。你几乎永远都不该传入 stx——也就是宏所转换的整块语法。你应该传入更具体的一小块语法，例如用户提供给宏的一个标识符。在这个例子中，我们使用 #'a。生成的标识符将与用户提供的那个标识符具有相同的作用域。这样更有可能符合用户的预期，尤其是当我们的宏与其他宏组合使用时。The first argument of format-id, lctx, is the lexical context of the identifier that will be created. You almost never want to supply stx—the overall chunk of syntax that the macro transforms. Instead you want to supply some more-specific bit of syntax, such as an identifier that the user has provided to the macro. In this example, we’re using #'a. The resulting identifier will have the same scope as that which the user provided. This is more likely to behave as the user expects, especially when our macro is composed with other macros.

4.1.4 另一个例子4.1.4 Another example

最后，这里有一个变体，可以接收任意数量的名字片段，再用连字符连接起来：Finally, here’s a variation that accepts an arbitrary number of name parts to be joined with hyphens:

> (require (for-syntax racket/string racket/syntax))
> (define-syntax (hyphen-define* stx)
    (syntax-case stx ()
      [(_ (names ...) (args ...) body0 body ...)
       (let ([name-stxs (syntax->list #'(names ...))])
         (with-syntax ([name (datum->syntax (car name-stxs)
                                            (string->symbol
                                             (string-join (for/list ([name-stx name-stxs])
                                                            (symbol->string
                                                             (syntax-e name-stx)))
                                                          "-")))])
           #'(define (name args ...)
               body0 body ...)))]))
> (hyphen-define* (foo bar baz) (v) (* 2 v))
> (foo-bar-baz 50)

100

和使用 format-id 时一样，使用 datum->syntax 时，我们也会谨慎处理第一个参数 lctx。我们希望所创建的标识符使用用户提供给宏的某个标识符的词法上下文。在这里，用户的标识符位于模板变量 (names ...) 中。我们把它从一个 syntax 转换成一个由多个 syntax 组成的 list。我们用第一个元素来提供词法上下文。当然，随后还会用全部元素来构造带连字符的标识符。Just as when we used format-id, when using datum->syntax we’re being careful with the first, lctx argument. We want the identifier we create to use the lexical context of an identifier provided to the macro by the user. In this case, the user’s identifiers are in the (names ...) template variable. We change this from one syntax into a list of syntaxes. The first element we use for the lexical context. Then of course we’ll use all the elements to form the hyphenated identifier.

回顾一下：To review:

  • 你不能在模板之外使用模式变量。但你可以对模式变量使用 syntax 或 #'，就地创建一个“迷你装”模板。You can’t use a pattern variable outside of a template. But you can use syntax or #' on a pattern variable to make an ad hoc, "fun size" template.

  • 如果你想对模式变量做些加工，再用到模板中，with-syntax 就是你的好帮手，因为它能让你创建新的模式变量。If you want to munge pattern variables for use in the template, with-syntax is your friend, because it lets you create new pattern variables.

  • 通常，你需要使用 syntax->datum 才能取得里面真正关心的值。Usually you’ll need to use syntax->datum to get the interesting value inside.

  • 用 format-id 格式化标识符名字很方便。format-id is convenient for formatting identifier names.

4.2 打造我们自己的 struct4.2 Making our own struct

让我们把刚学到的东西用到一个更贴近实际的例子中。假装 Racket 还没有 struct 功能。幸好，我们可以编写一个宏，提供一套自己的结构定义和使用机制。为简单起见，我们的结构将是不可变的（只读），而且不支持继承。Let’s apply what we just learned to a more-realistic example. We’ll pretend that Racket doesn’t already have a struct capability. Fortunately, we can write a macro to provide our own system for defining and using structures. To keep things simple, our structure will be immutable (read-only) and it won’t support inheritance.

给定这样一个结构声明：Given a structure declaration like:

(our-struct name (field1 field2 ...))

我们需要定义几个过程：We need to define some procedures:

  • 一个构造过程，其名字就是结构名。我们将用 vector 来表示结构。第 0 个元素是结构名，第 1 个及之后的元素是各个字段。A constructor procedure whose name is the struct name. We’ll represent structures as a vector. The structure name will be element zero. The fields will be elements one onward.

  • 一个判定过程，其名字是在结构名后面加上 ?。A predicate, whose name is the struct name with ? appended.

  • 为每个字段定义一个访问器过程，用来获取该字段的值。它们的名字将是 struct-field（结构名、一个连字符，再加上字段名）。For each field, an accessor procedure to get its value. These will be named struct-field (the name of the struct, a hyphen, and the field name).

> (require (for-syntax racket/syntax))
> (define-syntax (our-struct stx)
    (syntax-case stx ()
      [(_ id (fields ...))
       (with-syntax ([pred-id (format-id #'id "~a?" #'id)])
         #`(begin
             ; Define a constructor.
             (define (id fields ...)
               (apply vector (cons 'id  (list fields ...))))
             ; Define a predicate.
             (define (pred-id v)
               (and (vector? v)
                    (eq? (vector-ref v 0) 'id)))
             ; Define an accessor for each field.
             #,@(for/list ([x (syntax->list #'(fields ...))]
                           [n (in-naturals 1)])
                  (with-syntax ([acc-id (format-id #'id "~a-~a" #'id x)]
                                [ix n])
                    #`(define (acc-id v)
                        (unless (pred-id v)
                          (error 'acc-id "~a is not a ~a struct" v 'id))
                        (vector-ref v ix))))))]))
; Test it out
> (require rackunit)
> (our-struct foo (a b))
> (define s (foo 1 2))
> (check-true (foo? s))
> (check-false (foo? 1))
> (check-equal? (foo-a s) 1)
> (check-equal? (foo-b s) 2)
> (check-exn exn:fail?
             (lambda () (foo-a "furble")))
; The tests passed.
; Next, what if someone tries to declare:
> (our-struct "blah" ("blah" "blah"))

format-id: contract violation

  expected: (or/c string? symbol? identifier? keyword? char?

number?)

  given: #<syntax:eval:83:0 "blah">

这条错误消息帮助不大。它来自 format-id，而那是我们的宏内部私有的实现细节。The error message is not very helpful. It’s coming from format-id, which is a private implementation detail of our macro.

你可能知道，syntax-case 子句可以带一个可选的“守卫”（guard，也叫 fender）表达式。不一定非得这样写：You may know that a syntax-case clause can take an optional "guard" or "fender" expression. Instead of

[pattern template]

也可以这样写：It can be:

[pattern guard template]

我们给这个子句加上一个守卫表达式：Let’s add a guard expression to our clause:

> (require (for-syntax racket/syntax))
> (define-syntax (our-struct stx)
    (syntax-case stx ()
      [(_ id (fields ...))
       ; Guard or "fender" expression:
       (for-each (lambda (x)
                   (unless (identifier? x)
                     (raise-syntax-error #f "not an identifier" stx x)))
                 (cons #'id (syntax->list #'(fields ...))))
       (with-syntax ([pred-id (format-id #'id "~a?" #'id)])
         #`(begin
             ; Define a constructor.
             (define (id fields ...)
               (apply vector (cons 'id  (list fields ...))))
             ; Define a predicate.
             (define (pred-id v)
               (and (vector? v)
                    (eq? (vector-ref v 0) 'id)))
             ; Define an accessor for each field.
             #,@(for/list ([x (syntax->list #'(fields ...))]
                           [n (in-naturals 1)])
                  (with-syntax ([acc-id (format-id #'id "~a-~a" #'id x)]
                                [ix n])
                    #`(define (acc-id v)
                        (unless (pred-id v)
                          (error 'acc-id "~a is not a ~a struct" v 'id))
                        (vector-ref v ix))))))]))
; Now the same misuse gives a better error message:
> (our-struct "blah" ("blah" "blah"))

eval:86:0: our-struct: not an identifier

  at: "blah"

  in: (our-struct "blah" ("blah" "blah"))

后面我们会看到，syntax-parse 能让检查用法、针对错误提供有帮助的消息变得更加容易。Later, we’ll see how syntax-parse makes it even easier to check usage and provide helpful messages about mistakes.

4.3 用点号表示法查询嵌套哈希表4.3 Using dot notation for nested hash lookups

前两个例子用宏来定义函数，函数名是把传给宏的标识符连接起来得到的。这个例子则反过来：把传给宏的标识符拆成几个部分。The previous two examples used a macro to define functions whose names were made by joining identifiers provided to the macro. This example does the opposite: The identifier given to the macro is split into pieces.

如果你为 Web 服务编写程序，就会接触 JSON，它在 Racket 中用 jsexpr? 来表示。JSON 经常会有包含其他字典的字典。在 jsexpr? 中，它们由嵌套的 hasheq 表来表示：If you write programs for web services you deal with JSON, which is represented in Racket by a jsexpr?. JSON often has dictionaries that contain other dictionaries. In a jsexpr? these are represented by nested hasheq tables:

; Nested ‘hasheq's typical of a jsexpr:
> (define js (hasheq 'a (hasheq 'b (hasheq 'c "value"))))

在 JavaScript 中，你可以使用点号表示法：In JavaScript you can use dot notation:

foo = js.a.b.c;

在 Racket 中就没这么方便了：In Racket it’s not so convenient:

(hash-ref (hash-ref (hash-ref js 'a) 'b) 'c)

我们可以写一个辅助函数，让代码稍微清爽一些：We can write a helper function to make this a bit cleaner:

; This helper function:
> (define/contract (hash-refs h ks [def #f])
    ((hash? (listof any/c)) (any/c) . ->* . any)
    (with-handlers ([exn:fail? (const (cond [(procedure? def) (def)]
                                            [else def]))])
      (for/fold ([h h])
        ([k (in-list ks)])
        (hash-ref h k))))
; Lets us say:
> (hash-refs js '(a b c))

"value"

这样好多了。我们能否再进一步，使用有点像 JavaScript 的点号表示法呢？That’s better. Can we go even further and use a dot notation somewhat like JavaScript?

; This macro:
> (require (for-syntax racket/syntax))
> (define-syntax (hash.refs stx)
    (syntax-case stx ()
      ; If the optional ‘default' is missing, use #f.
      [(_ chain)
       #'(hash.refs chain #f)]
      [(_ chain default)
       (let* ([chain-str (symbol->string (syntax->datum #'chain))]
              [ids (for/list ([str (in-list (regexp-split #rx"\\." chain-str))])
                     (format-id #'chain "~a" str))])
         (with-syntax ([hash-table (car ids)]
                       [keys       (cdr ids)])
           #'(hash-refs hash-table 'keys default)))]))
; Gives us "sugar" to say this:
> (hash.refs js.a.b.c)

"value"

; Try finding a key that doesn't exist:
> (hash.refs js.blah)

#f

; Try finding a key that doesn't exist, specifying the default:
> (hash.refs js.blah 'did-not-exist)

'did-not-exist

成功了！It works!

我们已经开始意识到，宏被错误使用时，应该给出有帮助的消息。我们就在这里试着做到这一点。We’ve started to appreciate that our macros should give helpful messages when used in error. Let’s try to do that here.

> (require (for-syntax racket/syntax))
> (define-syntax (hash.refs stx)
    (syntax-case stx ()
      ; Check for no args at all
      [(_)
       (raise-syntax-error #f "Expected hash.key0[.key1 ...] [default]" stx)]
      ; If the optional ‘default' is missing, use #f.
      [(_ chain)
       #'(hash.refs chain #f)]
      [(_ chain default)
       (unless (identifier? #'chain)
         (raise-syntax-error #f "Expected hash.key0[.key1 ...] [default]" stx #'chain))
       (let* ([chain-str (symbol->string (syntax->datum #'chain))]
              [ids (for/list ([str (in-list (regexp-split #rx"\\." chain-str))])
                     (format-id #'chain "~a" str))])
         ; Check that we have at least hash.key
         (unless (and (>= (length ids) 2)
                      (not (eq? (syntax-e (cadr ids)) '||)))
           (raise-syntax-error #f "Expected hash.key" stx #'chain))
         (with-syntax ([hash-table (car ids)]
                       [keys       (cdr ids)])
           #'(hash-refs hash-table 'keys default)))]))
; See if we catch each of the misuses
> (hash.refs)

eval:97:0: hash.refs: Expected hash.key0[.key1 ...]

[default]

  in: (hash.refs)

> (hash.refs 0)

eval:98:0: hash.refs: Expected hash.key0[.key1 ...]

[default]

  at: 0

  in: (hash.refs 0 #f)

> (hash.refs js)

eval:99:0: hash.refs: Expected hash.key

  at: js

  in: (hash.refs js #f)

> (hash.refs js.)

eval:100:0: hash.refs: Expected hash.key

  at: js.

  in: (hash.refs js. #f)

还不错。当然，加上错误检查之后，版本就长了不少。错误检查代码往往会掩盖逻辑，这里也是如此。幸好，我们很快就会看到，syntax-parse 如何帮助缓解这个问题，就像普通 Racket 中的契约或 Typed Racket 中的类型所做的那样。Not too bad. Of course, the version with error-checking is quite a bit longer. Error-checking code generally tends to obscure the logic, and does here. Fortunately we’ll soon see how syntax-parse can help mitigate that, in much the same way as contracts in normal Racket or types in Typed Racket.

也许我们并不觉得，写 (hash.refs js.a.b.c) 就真的比 (hash-refs js '(a b c)) 更清楚。也许我们实际上不会使用这种方法。但 Racket 的宏系统让它成为一种可行的选择。Maybe we’re not convinced that writing (hash.refs js.a.b.c) is really clearer than (hash-refs js '(a b c)). Maybe we won’t actually use this approach. But the Racket macro system makes it a possible choice.

5 语法参数5 Syntax parameters

“回指式 if”（anaphoric if），也叫“aif”，是一个很流行的宏示例。不必这样写："Anaphoric if" or "aif" is a popular macro example. Instead of writing:

(let ([tmp (big-long-calculation)])
  (if tmp
      (foo tmp)
      #f))

你可以这样写：You could write:

(aif (big-long-calculation)
     (foo it)
     #f)

换句话说，当条件为真时，会自动创建一个 it 标识符，并将其设为条件表达式的值。这应该很容易：In other words, when the condition is true, an it identifier is automatically created and set to the value of the condition. This should be easy:

> (define-syntax-rule (aif condition true-expr false-expr)
    (let ([it condition])
      (if it
          true-expr
          false-expr)))
> (aif #t (displayln it) (void))

it: undefined;

 cannot reference an identifier before its definition

  in module: 'program

等等，什么？it 未定义？Wait, what? it is undefined?

原来，一直以来，我们都受到保护，避免在宏中犯某一类错误。所谓这类错误，就是我们的新语法引入了一个变量，而它意外地与宏周围代码中的变量发生了冲突。It turns out that all along we have been protected from making a certain kind of mistake in our macros. The mistake is if our new syntax introduces a variable that accidentally conflicts with one in the code surrounding our macro.

《Racket 参考手册》的“转换器绑定”一节有很好的解释和示例。基本上，语法带有“标记”，用来保持词法作用域。这使得宏在词法作用域方面的行为与普通函数一样。The Racket Reference section, Transformer Bindings, has a good explanation and example. Basically, syntax has "marks" to preserve lexical scope. This makes your macro behave like a normal function, for lexical scoping.

如果一个普通函数定义了名为 x 的变量，它不会与外层作用域中名为 x 的变量发生冲突：If a normal function defines a variable named x, it won’t conflict with a variable named x in an outer scope:

> (let ([x "outer"])
    (let ([x "inner"])
      (printf "The inner `x' is ~s\n" x))
    (printf "The outer `x' is ~s\n" x))

The inner `x' is "inner"

The outer `x' is "outer"

当我们的宏也遵守词法作用域规则时，就更容易写出行为可预测的可靠宏。When our macros also respect lexical scoping, it’s easier to write reliable macros that behave predictably.

所以，这是一种很棒的默认行为。但有时候，我们就是想刻意引入一个神奇的变量——比如 aif 中的 it。So that’s wonderful default behavior. But sometimes we want to introduce a magic variable on purpose—such as it for aif.

要做到这一点，有一种坏办法，也有一种好办法。There’s a bad way to do this and a good way.

坏办法是使用 datum->syntax，因为要正确使用它很不容易。The bad way is to use datum->syntax, which is tricky to use correctly.

参见《用语法参数保持干净》（Keeping it Clean with Syntax Parameters，PDF）。See Keeping it Clean with Syntax Parameters (PDF).

好办法是采用语法参数，使用 define-syntax-parameter 和 syntax-parameterize。你可能已经很熟悉 Racket 中的普通参数了：The good way is with a syntax parameter, using define-syntax-parameter and syntax-parameterize. You’re probably familiar with regular parameters in Racket:

> (define current-foo (make-parameter "some default value"))
> (current-foo)

"some default value"

> (parameterize ([current-foo "I have a new value, for now"])
    (current-foo))

"I have a new value, for now"

> (current-foo)

"some default value"

那是一个普通参数。语法参数的工作方式与它类似。思路是：我们定义 it，让它默认表示一个错误。只有在我们的 aif 内部，它才具有有意义的值：That’s a normal parameter. The syntax variation works similarly. The idea is that we’ll define it to mean an error by default. Only inside of our aif will it have a meaningful value:

> (require racket/stxparam)
> (define-syntax-parameter it
    (lambda (stx)
      (raise-syntax-error (syntax-e stx) "can only be used inside aif")))
> (define-syntax-rule (aif condition true-expr false-expr)
    (let ([tmp condition])
      (if tmp
          (syntax-parameterize ([it (make-rename-transformer #'tmp)])
            true-expr)
          false-expr)))
> (aif 10 (displayln it) (void))

10

> (aif #f (displayln it) (void))

在 syntax-parameterize 内部，it 充当 tmp 的别名。这种别名行为由 make-rename-transformer 创建。Inside the syntax-parameterize, it acts as an alias for tmp. The alias behavior is created by make-rename-transformer.

如果我们试图在 aif 形式之外使用 it，而 it 也没有在别处定义，就会如我们所愿，得到一个错误：If we try to use it outside of an aif form, and it isn’t otherwise defined, we get an error like we want:

> (displayln it)

it: can only be used inside aif

不过，我们仍然可以在局部定义上下文中，把 it 定义为一个普通变量，例如：But we can still define it as a normal variable in local definition contexts like:

> (let ([it 10])
    it)

10

或者：or:

> (define (foo)
    (define it 10)
    it)
> (foo)

10

想深入了解，请参见《用语法参数保持干净》（Keeping it Clean with Syntax Parameters）。For a deeper look, see Keeping it Clean with Syntax Parameters.

6 splicing-let 有什么用？6 What’s the point of splicing-let?

我盯着 racket/splicing 琢磨了很久很久。它是干什么的？我为什么要用它？为什么它会出现在参考手册的“宏”一节中？I stared at racket/splicing for the longest time. What does it do? Why would I use it? Why is it in the Macros section of the reference?

第一步，在盒子上开个洞——不，是揭开它的神秘面纱。例如，这样使用 splicing-let：Step one, cut a hole in the box de-mythologize it. For example, using splicing-let like this:

> (require racket/splicing)
> (splicing-let ([x 0])
    (define (get-x)
      x))
; get-x is visible out here:
> (get-x)

0

; but x is not:
> x

x: undefined;

 cannot reference an identifier before its definition

  in module: 'program

等价于：is equivalent to:

> (define get-y
    (let ([y 0])
      (lambda ()
        y)))
; get-y is visible out here:
> (get-y)

0

; but y is not:
> y

y: undefined;

 cannot reference an identifier before its definition

  in module: 'program

这是经典的 Lisp/Scheme/Racket 惯用法，有时叫作“let 包着 lambda”（let over lambda）。闭包把 y 隐藏起来，只有通过 get-y 才能访问它。This is the classic Lisp/Scheme/Racket idiom sometimes called "let over lambda". A closure hides y, which can only be accessed via get-y.

一则关于闭包与对象的公案。A koan about closures and objects.

那么，我们为什么要关心这些拼接形式呢？它们可以更简洁，尤其是在主体中有多个形式时：So why would we care about the splicing forms? They can be more concise, especially when there are multiple body forms:

> (require racket/splicing)
> (splicing-let ([x 0])
    (define (inc)
      (set! x (+ x 1)))
    (define (dec)
      (set! x (- 1 x)))
    (define (get)
      x))

拼接版本比通常的写法更方便：The splicing variation is more convenient than the usual way:

> (define-values (inc dec get)
    (let ([x 0])
      (values (lambda ()  ; inc
                (set! x (+ x 1)))
              (lambda ()  ; dec
                (set! x (- x 1)))
              (lambda ()  ; get
                x))))

当主体中有很多形式，而且我们要在宏中生成这些形式时，使用拼接版本可以轻松得多。When there are many body forms—and we’re generating them in a macro—the splicing variations can be much easier.

7 健壮的宏：syntax-parse7 Robust macros: syntax-parse

函数可能被用错。宏也一样。Functions can be used in error. So can macros.

7.1 函数的错误处理策略7.1 Error-handling strategies for functions

对于普普通通的函数，我们有几种处理误用的选择。With plain old functions, we have several choices how to handle misuse.

1. 完全不检查。1. Don’t check at all.

> (define (misuse s)
    (string-append s " snazzy suffix"))
; User of the function:
> (misuse 0)

string-append: contract violation

  expected: string?

  given: 0

  argument position: 1st

  other arguments...:

   " snazzy suffix"

; I guess I goofed, but – what is this "string-append" of which you
; speak??

问题在于，由此产生的错误消息会令人困惑。用户以为自己调用的是 misuse，得到的却是来自 string-append 的错误消息。在这个简单的例子里，他们或许能猜出发生了什么，但大多数情况下都猜不出来。The problem is that the resulting error message will be confusing. Our user thinks they’re calling misuse, but they’re getting an error message from string-append. In this simple example they could probably guess what’s happening, but in most cases they won’t.

2. 编写一些错误处理代码。2. Write some error handling code.

> (define (misuse s)
    (unless (string? s)
      (error 'misuse "expected a string, but got ~a" s))
    (string-append s " snazzy suffix"))
; User of the function:
> (misuse 0)

misuse: expected a string, but got 0

; I goofed, and understand why! It's a shame the writer of the
; function had to work so hard to tell me.

遗憾的是，错误处理代码往往会喧宾夺主，甚至掩盖函数定义本身。另外，错误消息虽然不错，却还不够好。要进一步改善它，就需要更多错误处理代码。Unfortunately the error code tends to overwhelm and/or obscure our function definition. Also, the error message is good but not great. Improving it would require even more error code.

3. 使用契约。3. Use a contract.

> (define/contract (misuse s)
    (string? . -> . string?)
    (string-append s " snazzy suffix"))
; User of the function:
> (misuse 0)

misuse: contract violation

  expected: string?

  given: 0

  in: the 1st argument of

      (-> string? string?)

  contract from: (function misuse)

  blaming: program

   (assuming the contract is correct)

  at: eval:131.0

; I goofed, and understand why! I'm happier, and I hear the writer of
; the function is happier, too.

这种办法两全其美。This is the best of both worlds.

契约简单而简洁。更棒的是，它是声明式的。我们说的是希望发生什么，而不是如何实现。The contract is simple and concise. Even better, it’s declarative. We say what we want to happen, not how.

另一方面，函数的用户会得到非常详细的错误消息。而且，消息采用的是标准、熟悉的格式。On the other hand the user of our function gets a very detailed error message. Plus, the message is in a standard, familiar format.

4. 使用 Typed Racket。4. Use Typed Racket.

#lang typed/racket
> (: misuse (String -> String))
> (define (misuse s)
    (string-append s " snazzy suffix"))
> (misuse 0)

eval:3:0: Type Checker: type mismatch

  expected: String

  given: Zero

  in: 0

更进一步，Typed Racket 可以在编译时就提前发现用法错误。Even better, Typed Racket can catch usage mistakes up-front at compile time.

7.2 宏的错误处理策略7.2 Error-handling strategies for macros

对于宏，我们也有类似的选择。For macros, we have similar choices.

1. 忽略误用的可能性。对于宏来说，这个选择更加糟糕。默认的错误消息更难让人看懂，更不用说帮助用户知道该怎么办了。1. Ignore the possibility of misuse. This choice is even worse for macros. The default error messages are even less likely to make sense, much less help our user know what to do.

2. 编写错误处理代码。在“用点号表示法查询嵌套哈希表”的例子中，我们已经看到，这会让宏变得多么复杂。而在我们还在学习如何编写宏的时候，尤其不希望增加认知负担，让代码变得晦涩难懂。2. Write error-handling code. We saw how much this complicated our macros in our example of Using dot notation for nested hash lookups. And while we’re still learning how to write macros, we especially don’t want more cognitive load and obfuscation.

3. 使用 syntax-parse。对宏而言，这相当于对函数使用契约或类型。我们可以声明，输入模式中的元素必须是某一类东西，比如标识符。这些类别不叫“类型”，而叫“语法类”。系统提供了一些预定义的语法类，我们也可以定义自己的语法类。3. Use syntax-parse. For macros, this is the equivalent of using contracts or types for functions. We can declare that input pattern elements must be certain kinds of things, such as an identifier. Instead of "types", the kinds are referred to as "syntax classes". There are predefined syntax classes, plus we can define our own.

7.3 使用 syntax-parse7.3 Using syntax-parse

2012 年 11 月 1 日：事情是这样的。写完前面这些内容之后，我坐下来重新阅读了 syntax-parse 的文档。它……非常好懂。我并没有感到困惑。November 1, 2012: So here’s the deal. After writing everything up to this point, I sat down to re-read the documentation for syntax-parse. It was...very understandable. I didn’t feel confused.

为什么呢？文档有一篇很不错的“引言”，包含许多简单的例子，后面还有一个“示例”部分，展示了许多实际应用场景。Why? The documentation has a nice Introduction with many simple examples, followed by an Examples section illustrating many real-world scenarios.

更新：此外，Ben Greenman 创建了一个包，其文档提供了更多出色的“Syntax Parse 示例”。Update: Furthermore, Ben Greenman has created a package whose docs provide an excellent set of even more Syntax Parse Examples.

另外，到目前为止学到的一切，都让我有了足够的准备，能够理解 syntax-parse 做了什么，以及为什么这样做。至少到现在为止，具体用法看起来都相当直观。Furthermore, everything I’d learned up to this point prepared me to appreciate what syntax-parse does, and why. The details of how to use it seem pretty straightforward, so far.

这很可能只是我暂时处于“不知道自己不知道什么”的状态。随着深入探索、更多地使用它，也许我会发现一些令人困惑或棘手的地方。如果真有那么一天，我会回来更新这里的内容。This might well be a temporary state of me "not knowing what I don’t know". As I dig in and use it more, maybe I’ll discover something confusing or tricky. If/when I do, I’ll come back here and update this.

不过，目前我会把精力放在改进前面的部分上。But for now I’ll focus on improving the previous parts.

8 参考资料与致谢8 References and Acknowledgments

Eli Barzilay 的博文《编写 ‘syntax-case’ 宏》（Writing ‘syntax-case’ Macros）帮助我理解了许多关键细节和概念，也启发我采用“自底向上”的讲解方式。Eli Barzilay’s blog post, Writing ‘syntax-case’ Macros, helped me understand many key details and concepts, and inspired me to use a "bottom-up" approach.

Eli 还写了另一篇博文《看起来不太干净的卫生机制》（Dirty Looking Hygiene），解释了 syntax-parameterize。我大量参考了这篇文章，主要只是做了些更新，因为他写文章时，PLT Scheme 还没有改名为 Racket。Eli wrote another blog post, Dirty Looking Hygiene, which explains syntax-parameterize. I relied heavily on that, mostly just updating it since his post was written before PLT Scheme was renamed to Racket.

Matthew Flatt 的《可组合、可编译的宏：你到底什么时候要它？》（Composable and Compilable Macros: You Want it When?，PDF）解释了 Racket 如何处理编译时与运行时的区别。Matthew Flatt’s Composable and Compilable Macros: You Want it When? (PDF) explains how Racket handles compile time vs. run time.

Kent Dybvig 所著《Scheme 程序设计语言》（The Scheme Programming Language）的第 8 章解释了 syntax-rules 和 syntax-case。Chapter 8 of The Scheme Programming Language by Kent Dybvig explains syntax-rules and syntax-case.

《加固宏》（Fortifying Macros，PDF）是 Ryan Culpepper 和 Matthias Felleisen 介绍 syntax-parse 的论文。Fortifying Macros (PDF) is the paper by Ryan Culpepper and Matthias Felleisen introducing syntax-parse.

Shriram Krishnamurthi 看过一份很早期的草稿，并鼓励我继续写下去。Sam Tobin-Hochstadt 和 Robby Findler 也给了我鼓励。Matthew Flatt 教我如何让 Scribble 的 interaction 把 syntax 打印为 "syntax"，而不是 "#'"。Jay McCarthy 帮我找出了一些错误和混淆之处。Jon Rafkind 提供了一些建议。Kieron Hardy 报告了一个字体问题和一些拼写错误。Shriram Krishnamurthi looked at a very early draft and encouraged me to keep going. Sam Tobin-Hochstadt and Robby Findler also encouraged me. Matthew Flatt showed me how to make a Scribble interaction print syntax as "syntax" rather than as "#'". Jay McCarthy helped me catch some mistakes and confusions. Jon Rafkind provided suggestions. Kieron Hardy reported a font issue and some typos.

最后，我注意到一件奇怪的事。写完这里的大部分内容之后，我重新读了一些 Racket 文档，发现它们比我上次阅读时进步了。当然，文档还是原来的文档；变的是我。有趣的是，我们会把自己已经知道的许多东西投射到字里行间。我的意思是，Racket 的文档非常好。《指南》提供了有帮助的示例和教程。《参考手册》则非常清晰、精确。Finally, I noticed something strange. After writing much of this, when I returned to some parts of the Racket documentation, I noticed it had improved since I last read it. Of course, it was the same; I’d changed. It’s interesting how much of what we already know is projected between the lines. My point is, the Racket documentation is very good. The Guide provides helpful examples and tutorials. The Reference is very clear and precise.
